scenarios.name: Project Overview Content Validation
scenarios.description: Validate that the hero section and project overview clearly communicate MirDB's purpose as a persistent key-value store with Memcached protocol support

steps.description: Open the root URL of the website in a browser

steps.action: Verify hero section contains value proposition
steps.description: Check that the hero section includes a clear one-line description identifying MirDB as a persistent key-value store with Memcached protocol support
Confirm that the hero or hero-adjacent section displays the top 3 differentiating features: persistence, LSM tree architecture, and Memcached compatibility

test_cases.expected: Hero section displays clear one-line value proposition: MirDB is a persistent key-value store with Memcached protocol support

test_cases.input: View hero section or feature highlights section
test_cases.expected: Hero section displays all three key differentiators: persistence, LSM tree architecture, and Memcached compatibility

scenarios.name: Feature Highlights Presentation
scenarios.description: Validate that all core MirDB features are highlighted with clear explanations and visual representation of key features

steps.description: Scroll to or navigate to the feature highlights/Features section of the homepage

steps.action: Verify Memcached Protocol Compatibility feature is displayed
steps.description: Check that feature highlight explains existing memcached clients can be used

steps.action: Verify Persistent Storage feature is displayed
steps.description: Check that feature highlight explains data survives restarts unlike pure memcached

steps.action: Verify LSM Tree Architecture feature is displayed
steps.description: Check that feature highlight explains efficient write-optimized storage
Check that feature highlight shows tunable parameters for different workloads

test_cases.expected: Descriptions for each feature highlight: 1) Memcached Protocol Compatibility - Can use existing memcached clients, 2) Persistent Storage - Data survives restarts, 3) LSM Tree Architecture - Efficient write-optimized storage, 4) Configurable - Tunable parameters for different workloads

scenarios.name: Architecture Visualization and Data Flow
scenarios.description: Validate that architecture diagrams clearly show the LSM tree data flow from WAL through memtables to SSTable levels

steps.description: Locate and open the architecture section from navigation menu
Confirm that an architecture diagram is visible showing data flow components
Verify diagram shows WAL → Memtable → Immutable Memtables → SSTable Levels flow
Confirm diagram illustrates the LSM tree compaction process and level organization
steps.context: Architecture diagram with data flow components visible

test_cases.expected: Architecture diagram shows clear data flow from WAL → Memtable → Immutable Memtables → Level 0 SSTs → Level 1+ SSTs
Diagram and explanation clearly illustrate the LSM tree compaction process and sorted, non-overlapping SSTable levels

scenarios.name: Getting Started Guide and Quick Start
scenarios.description: Verify that the getting started guide provides installation instructions and basic usage examples that work within 5 minutes

steps.description: Locate and open the getting started/quick start section from navigation
Check that instructions include: 1) Prerequisites, 2) Clone repository command, 3) Build command (e.g., cargo build --release), 4) Run command with default configuration

steps.action: Verify basic usage examples with expected outputs
steps.description: Check that SET/GET/DELETE commands are shown with correct syntax and example output
Measure time to complete installation and run basic commands
steps.context: New terminal session in appropriate directory

test_cases.expected: Complete step-by-step instructions including: Prerequisites section (Rust toolchain, Git), Clone command (git clone <repo-url>), Build command (cargo build --release), Run command (./target/release/mirdb --config config.toml)

test_cases.input: Follow installation instructions step by step
test_cases.expected: Commands execute successfully: git clone, cargo build --release completes without errors, and ./target/release/mirdb starts the server within 5 minutes timeout

test_cases.input: Execute example SET/GET commands from documentation
test_cases.expected: Commands work as documented: telnet localhost 12333 can connect, SET key1 value1 stores data, GET key1 retrieves 'value1', DELETE key1 removes key successfully

scenarios.name: Memcached Command Documentation
scenarios.description: Validate that all supported Memcached commands are documented with examples showing syntax, parameters, and expected outputs

steps.description: Locate commands/API documentation in site navigation

steps.action: Verify standard Memcached commands are documented
steps.description: Check for documentation of SET, GET, GETS, DELETE, ADD, REPLACE, APPEND, PREPEND commands
Check for documentation of INFO and MAJOR_COMPACTION commands

steps.action: Verify command examples show syntax and output
steps.description: Confirm each command includes: syntax format, parameter descriptions, example input, and example output

test_cases.expected: Documentation shows all 8 standard Memcached commands: SET, GET, GETS, DELETE, ADD, REPLACE, APPEND, PREPEND with descriptions
Documentation includes INFO and MAJOR_COMPACTION commands with explanations of MirDB-specific functionality
SET command shows: syntax (SET <key> <flags> <exptime> <bytes> [noreply]\r\n<data>\r\n), parameters table explaining each field, example input, example response (STORED or ERROR)

scenarios.name: Configuration Documentation
scenarios.description: Validate that configurable parameters are organized by category with descriptions, default values, and acceptable formats

steps.description: Locate configuration guide in site navigation
Check that parameters are grouped logically: Network, Storage, Memory Tables, SSTables, Compaction

steps.action: Verify each parameter has complete documentation
steps.description: For each parameter, verify: parameter name, description, default value, acceptable formats/values, and configuration file syntax example
steps.context: Configuration categories visible with parameter lists

steps.action: Verify default configuration values match knowledge base
steps.description: Check that defaults match: Listen Address (0.0.0.0:12333), Max LSM Levels (7), Work Directory (/tmp/mirdb), SSTable Max Size (100MB), Memtable Max Size (4MB), Block Size (4KB)

test_cases.expected: Parameters are organized into clear categories: 1) Network (listen_addr, max_connections), 2) Storage (work_dir, data_dir, wal_dir), 3) Memory Tables (memtable_max_size, memtable_max_count), 4) SSTables (sstable_max_size, block_size, bloom_filter_bits_per_key), 5) Compaction (minor_compaction_threshold, major_compaction_interval, max_lsm_levels)
Default values displayed and accurate: listen_addr = 0.0.0.0:12333, max_lsm_levels = 7, work_dir = /tmp/mirdb, sstable_max_size = 100MB, memtable_max_size = 4MB, block_size = 4KB
Example configuration file or snippet shown with proper syntax (TOML format as per knowledge base)

scenarios.name: Repository Navigation and Links
scenarios.description: Validate that source code repository is accessible via prominent links that open in new tabs

steps.action: Check header navigation for repository link
steps.description: Look for repository/GitHub link in the site's header/navigation bar
Verify repository link is present in website footer

steps.action: Verify link opens in new tab
steps.description: Check that repository links have target='_blank' and rel='noopener noreferrer' attributes

steps.action: Verify link points to correct repository
steps.description: Confirm the link URL matches the MirDB source repository location (e.g., GitHub/GitLab URL)

test_cases.input: Inspect website header and footer for repository links
test_cases.expected: At least one prominent repository link visible in header OR a consistent link in footer
Link has target='_blank' attribute to open in new tab AND rel='noopener noreferrer' for security
Link URL points to valid and accessible source code repository (e.g., https://github.com/example/mirdb)

scenarios.name: Responsive Design and Mobile Compatibility
scenarios.description: Validate that the website displays correctly across different viewport sizes including mobile and desktop

steps.description: View website at standard desktop resolution and verify all content is readable and accessible
View website at tablet resolution and verify layout adapts appropriately
View website at mobile resolution and verify layout adapts, navigation is accessible, and text is readable
On mobile viewport, check that navigation menu collapses to hamburger menu or adjusts appropriately

steps.action: Verify touch target sizes on mobile
steps.description: Check that all clickable elements (links, buttons, navigation) have minimum 44x44px touch target on mobile

test_cases.expected: All content displays clearly: hero section readable, feature highlights in grid or appropriate layout, navigation spaced properly
Layout adapts gracefully: feature highlights stack appropriately, code blocks remain readable, navigation adjusts
Content is readable on mobile: text size appropriate, horizontal scrolling minimized, navigation accessible via menu

test_cases.input: Verify touch target sizes on mobile
test_cases.expected: All interactive elements have minimum 44x44px touch area, meeting WCAG and mobile UX standards

scenarios.name: Performance and Page Load Times
scenarios.description: Validate that website loads within 3 seconds on standard connections and passes performance audits

steps.action: Measure page load time from navigation start
steps.description: Use browser developer tools network tab or performance API to measure initial page load time
steps.context: Website deployed to production or staging

steps.description: Use Google Lighthouse in browser DevTools to audit performance score and metrics
Check that images are optimized, CSS/JS is minified, and assets are served with appropriate caching headers
Confirm that above-the-fold content renders within acceptable time, even if below-the-fold content loads later

test_cases.expected: Page completes load within 3 seconds on standard broadband connection (3G fast or 4G throttled in dev tools)
Lighthouse performance score is 90 or higher, meeting NFR-1 requirements
Images optimized (WebP format where supported, appropriate sizes), CSS/JS minified, caching headers configured for static assets

scenarios.name: SEO and Accessibility Compliance
scenarios.description: Validate that the website is SEO-optimized with appropriate meta tags and follows accessibility guidelines

steps.description: View page source and verify presence of title tag, meta description, Open Graph tags (og:title, og:description, og:image), Twitter card. Description should include 'MirDB', 'persistent key-value store', 'Memcached protocol', 'LSM tree' for SEO
Check that HTML uses semantic elements: <nav>, <main>, <section>, <article>, <footer>, proper heading hierarchy (h1 → h2 → h3)
steps.context: Page source or DOM inspector open

steps.description: Use browser extension or DevTools to verify color contrast meets WCAG 2.1 Level AA minimum of 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text

steps.action: Verify alt text for images and diagrams
steps.description: Check that all tags have descriptive alt attributes, particularly for architecture diagrams and feature icons
Navigate through the site using only keyboard (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter) to verify all interactive elements are accessible
Check for 'skip to main content' link at top of page for screen readers (visible on focus)

test_cases.expected: Title tag is 50-60 chars, includes 'MirDB'. Meta description is 150-160 chars, describes MirDB purpose. Open Graph tags: og:title, og:description, og:type=website, og:image present. Twitter card tags: twitter:card, twitter:title, twitter:description present

Uses semantic HTML5 elements throughout: <header> with <nav>, <main>, multiple <section> or <article> for feature items, <footer>. Heading hierarchy: single h1 for page title, h2 for main sections, h3 for subsections - no skipped levels
All text meets WCAG 2.1 Level AA: Normal text (body, paragraphs, code) has contrast ratio ≥ 4.5:1, Large text (headings ≥ 24px or 19px bold) has contrast ratio ≥ 3:1

test_cases.input: Verify alt text for all images
test_cases.expected: Every tag has descriptive alt attribute. Architecture diagrams have detailed alt describing data flow (WAL→Memtable→SSTables). Decorative images use alt=''. Icons have aria-label or title describing purpose

All interactive elements (navigation links, repository links, copy buttons, hamburger menu) are reachable via Tab, focus indicators visible, logical tab order follows visual flow, dropdown menus open with Enter/Space
Skip link present at beginning of DOM (before navigation), becomes visible when focused, links to main content anchor (#main-content or similar), reads clearly: 'Skip to main content'

scenarios.name: Code Syntax Highlighting and Copy Functionality
scenarios.description: Validate that code blocks have syntax highlighting for memcached commands and Rust code where applicable, plus copy-to-clipboard functionality

steps.action: View code blocks in getting started section
steps.description: Locate code examples with Rust build commands and memcached SET/GET commands
Confirm that command keywords, strings, comments, and parameters have different colors/styles
Check that each code block has a copy button (usually top-right corner)
Click copy button and verify command is copied to clipboard
steps.context: Code block with copy button present

steps.description: Check that code blocks have proper formatting: line numbers (optional), horizontal scrolling if needed, consistent indentation, monospace font

test_cases.input: Check syntax highlighting in memcached command examples
test_cases.expected: Memcached commands (SET, GET, DELETE, etc.) highlighted differently from values and keys, memcached protocol syntax has color differentiation. Rust code examples use Rust syntax highlighting if build command examples shown
Copy button visible on every code block, clicking button copies full code block content to clipboard, visual feedback provided (button text changes to 'Copied!' or checkmark appears temporarily)
Code blocks use monospace font, maintain indentation, have horizontal scrollbar if lines are long, background color differentiates from body text, inline code uses different styling than block code

scenarios.name: Project Status and Feature Implementation Tracking
scenarios.description: Verify that project status section shows implemented vs. planned features with clear status indicators

steps.description: Locate project status/roadmap section in site navigation
Check that implemented features are shown with 'Implemented' or checkmark status
Check that planned/in-progress features are shown with appropriate status indicators

steps.action: Verify feature completion percentages or progress indicators
steps.description: Check for progress bars, percentages, or clear visual indicators of implementation status

test_cases.expected: Page or section displays feature list with status: Implemented features include: Memcached protocol support (SET, GET, DELETE, etc.), LSM tree storage engine, WAL for durability, Memtable and immutable memtables, SSTable creation and management at multiple levels, Minor and major compaction, Basic configuration via TOML. All have 'Implemented' or ✓ status
Visual progress indicators shown: progress bars or percentage complete, color coding (green=implemented, yellow=in progress, gray=planned), last updated timestamp or version information

scenarios.name: Navigation and Site Structure
scenarios.description: Verify that website has sticky header with clear section links and logical site structure

steps.description: Scroll down the page and confirm header remains visible and functional

steps.action: Verify all main sections are in navigation
steps.description: Check that navigation includes links to: Home/Overview, Features, Architecture, Getting Started, Commands/API, Configuration, Project Status
Click each navigation link and verify it scrolls to or loads the correct section/page
Check that current section is highlighted in navigation as user scrolls or navigates

test_cases.expected: Header remains fixed at top of viewport, navigation stays accessible, no layout shift occurs
Navigation includes: Home/Overview, Features, Architecture, Getting Started, Commands (or API), Configuration, Project Status (or Roadmap)
